policy.ckNativeAnswer: Override WEAP.DNAM.Speed (Mutagen Weapon.Data.Speed) on each selected winning weapon record.
policy.whyCode: The selection is a deterministic rule over thousands of current load-order winners and must regenerate after weapon or load-order changes; hand-authoring 3,007 overrides is not reviewable or maintainable.
policy.sharedGeneratorDebt: The rule-over-many case justifies generation under CK-first rule 4, but the standalone .NET project should become a policy in the shared record-patch generator under rule 6.

priorArt.vanillaAndCk: Vanilla stores per-base-weapon speed in WEAP.DNAM.Speed and identifies the seven conventional classes with standard WeapType keywords; no global CK record applies a per-class policy to arbitrary later mod weapons.

exactCandidate.name: Weapon Stat Synthesis Patcher
exactCandidate.finding: Exact architecture: a configurable Synthesis patcher normalizing melee weapon stats across all mods. Version 1.2 allows non-speed stats to be disabled and supports named-weapon offsets and more weapon families.
exactCandidate.disposition: User decision required before replacement; this receipt does not choose between the installed narrow policy and the broader released patcher.

adjacentCandidates.name: Customize Weapon Speed
adjacentCandidates.difference: Papyrus/SKSE runtime mutation and name matching rather than a static override-only patch.

adjacentCandidates.name: Weapon Speed - IPM
adjacentCandidates.difference: Runtime IPM/MCM implementation with additional dependencies.

adjacentCandidates.name: Weapon Speed Mult Fix
adjacentCandidates.difference: Fixes WeaponSpeedMult actor-value stacking; it explicitly describes Customize Weapon Speed as changing a different parameter.

distribution.basis: The MIT generator/configuration is distributable. The generated override plugin copies winning third-party record data; override-only status does not itself grant redistribution rights, so the binary remains local-only until a concrete source-permissions review.

evidenceLimits: The original build's exact .NET SDK version was not logged; the new global.json pin prevents that omission on future rebuilds but cannot retroactively identify it.

Only the final plugin and package remain. The two original generation outputs asserted byte-identical in PR #179 were not both retained, so their equality cannot be independently replayed from two historical files.
The exact 2026-09-02 input list is retained locally and hashed but is intentionally ignored because it discloses the private load order; the public receipt records only its count and hash.
The installed 0.1.0 binary has not received a record-by-record redistribution-rights review and must not be published merely because it is override-only.
